Sysmon64 + SysmonDrv services both Running. detection_surface.process_creation_4688: ENABLED 2026-10-03 (was: No Auditing). auditpol now Success and Failure for Process Creation, Account Management, Task Scheduler, Registry.
detection_surface.implication: Only techniques that emit Security-channel events are verifiable. Anything needing 4688, Sysmon, or PowerShell 4104 is NOT detectable on this host as configured.

prerequisites.why: 4688 is the backbone of PowerShell/process detection. Currently OFF.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts - interactive logon as Administrator
detect: 67028 Special privileges assigned to new logon
techniques.notes: Every SSH session triggers this. Baseline noise, not an attack on its own.

techniques.name: Create Account: Local Account
techniques.command: New-LocalUser -Name 'ssop_lab_user' -NoPassword -FullName 'lab' -Description 'ssop atomic lab' -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Add-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Administrators' -Member 'ssop_lab_user' -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Output 'CREATED_AND_ELEVATED'
techniques.cleanup: Remove-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Administrators' -Member 'ssop_lab_user' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-LocalUser -Name 'ssop_lab_user' -ErrorAction Stop; if (Get-LocalUser -Name 'ssop_lab_user' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Write-Output 'STILL_THERE' } else { Write-Output 'REMOVED' }
techniques.notes: HIGH-VALUE. Creates a persistence account AND grants admin. VERIFIED 2026-10-03: fired on .78, Wazuh emitted 60109 (user account created) + 60110 (account changed) + 67027 (process created, 4688) at level 8. Use -NoPassword: this host's password policy rejects ConvertTo-SecureString values with InvalidPasswordException even when they meet apparent complexity.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task: recurring task
techniques.command: $a = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'cmd.exe' -Argument '/c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\ssop_task.txt'; $t = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date).AddMinutes(10); Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'ssop_lab_task' -Action $a -Trigger $t -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Write-Output REGISTERED
techniques.requires: auditpol: Detailed Tracking > Task Scheduler = Success
techniques.notes: Rule 60642 already fires on this host so detection is PROVEN, not theoretical.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.command: New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' -Name 'ssop_lab_persist' -Value 'C:\Windows\Temp\ssop_beacon.exe' -PropertyType String -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Write-Output SET
techniques.notes: Classic persistence. Low blast radius, easy cleanup.

techniques.name: LSASS Memory Access
techniques.command: $p = Get-Process lsass; $out = 'C:\Windows\Temp\ssop_lsass.dmp'; try { $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($p.Modules[0].FileName); Write-Output ('READ_ONLY_BYTES=' + $bytes.Length) } catch { Write-Output 'BLOCKED' }
detect: 10 access to lsass.exe (requires Sysmon - NOT PRESENT)
techniques.notes: DO NOT RUN without Sysmon. Would be undetectable here and touches credential material.

techniques.name: Brute Force: SSH from c2-sink
techniques.command: for i in $(seq 1 6); do timeout 4 ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=3 -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1 lab@192.168.1.78 wrong$i 2>/dev/null; done; echo BRUTE_DONE
techniques.notes: Attacker-side on .79, victim-side log on .78. Two agents see this one.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.command: for p in 22 135 139 445 3389 5985 5986; do timeout 2 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/192.168.1.78/$p" 2>/dev/null && echo "OPEN $p"; done; echo SCAN_DONE
techniques.notes: Establishes the service inventory Wazuh would alert on during recon.

ssop_chain_gap.observed: Wazuh detected the technique (level 8), but ssop-cases opened 0.
ssop_chain_gap.cause: router.py RULE_MAP has 23 mapped rules and NONE of them are the Windows rules this host emits (60109/60110/67027/60106/67028). Unmapped rules never classify, so they never become cases.
ssop_chain_gap.next: Map the Windows rule ids in RULE_MAP with an explicit category and level. Until then Windows detection is proven at the sensor but does not enter the SSOP decision chain.
ssop_chain_gap.resolved: RESOLVED 2026-10-03. RULE_MAP had 23 entries and none covered Windows, so unmapped Windows rules fell to DEFAULT_CATEGORY=operational. Firing T1136.001 minted a REAL tier-2 escalation from rule 60154 (Administrators Group Changed, L12). Mapped 30 Windows rule ids (20 explicitly + the ones the host actually emits); host now emits 30 distinct rules and 0 are unmapped. After a correct deploy, re-firing produced escalated 0 with cases still opening.
ssop_chain_gap.deploy_trap: The runtime layout is FLAT. deploy_runtime.sh copies agents/<f> -> $RT/<f>, so the live file is /home/rdrolfe/agent-runtime/router.py, not agents/router.py. Scp'ing to agents/ silently changes nothing.
